Raw values: room, color, early, richness, time 0..100; predelay and late reflection delay 0..150; level 1..100; byte 22 always 0x64, byte 18 always 00. routing_command.layout: 70 00 00 00 | 53 00 00 00 | 00 x8 | d3 41 | <group> | 32 x (source type, source index)
routing_command.notes: Changing the source of mixer strip 5 re-sent five frames, groups 06, 0a, 0b, 0c, 0d in that order, identical except for slots 16-31: 00 00 in group 06, 09 00 in the others. The same difference is in each group's own readback (category 0x03, index = group), so a write built from the readback with one slot changed reproduces the captured frames byte for byte. Slots 0-15 are the 16 mixer strips. Only slot 4 (strip 5) was changed in a capture. Changing strip 1's source did NOT send these frames: it sent one frame to group 09 (four slots, source type 00), so slots 0-3 here (04 00..04 03) are fixed feeds from the four effect-rack channels and group 09 picks what feeds each rack. 2026-11-22 vendor panel run: group 09 is the DAW page's Record 1-4 = the four rack inputs (one frame d3 41 09 <4 slots> per change, nothing else written), group 00 Line Out 1-4, 07 ADAT OUT 1-8, 08 SPDIF OUT 1-2; each change wrote only the touched group. Groups 1-5 (2 slots) were written by no panel control.

destination_groups.6, 10, 11, 12, 13: 32 slots each, one shared mixer strip source map: slots 0-15 = strips 1-16, slots 16-31 unused (00 00 in group 6, 09 00 in the rest). Record N (DAW page) and mixer strip N are the same slot.

routing_command.destination_sources_notes: The source kinds a new assignment may use per group (mute always). From the panel's menus: Line Out, ADAT and S/PDIF Out offer the seven non-loopback rows (sources other than MUTE written on Line Out 2 and S/PDIF Out 2; on ADAT Out only MUTE was picked, so its list is the menu's, a CANDIDATE for anything but MUTE); the DAW page (Record 1-8) adds the two loopbacks, allowed for group 09 where they were written. In the mixer map (groups 6, 10-13) they are not offered: the panel offers them only for Record 5-8, the map has no per-slot rule here, and a mix fed into one of its own strips is a feedback loop; a loopback already in the map is shown and re-sent unchanged. AFX OUT is in no menu.

readback.hazard: Same protocol family as the Orion, where an out-of-range index BusFaults the MCU (power cycle). Query only inside category_counts.

categories.0x03: routing, 14 records, each <group id> then (source type, source index) pairs; index = group id. Groups 6, 10, 11, 12, 13 are the mixer strip source map (see frame.routing_command). The others (body lengths 9, 5, 5, 5, 5, 5, -, 17, 5, 9) are not decoded.
categories.0x04: mixer, 4 records of 133 bytes, index = mix. Bytes 0-65 are 33 (fader, pan + flags) pairs: pair 0 read 00 20 and was never written, pairs 1-16 are strips 1-16 (see layouts), pairs 17-32 read like more strips and are not shown by the panel. Bytes 66-132 (60, then 33 pairs equal to category 0x18) are not decoded.
categories.0x07: per-effect instance state, queried only for loaded types (index 0x1b for Master De-esser; index 0 after ClearQ was loaded). Not bounded: do not query.
categories.0x0a: Gazelle Reverb config, 34 bytes: header 00, then 11-byte blocks; block 0 = the reverb (frame.auraverb_command).
categories.0x0b: link tables; the panel queries indices 0, 3 and 4 only: index 0 body[pair] preamp links, index 3 body[mix*16 + pair] mixer strip links, index 4 body[pair] rack links (2026-11-22 marker reopen). Not bounded: indices 1 and 2 were never queried and are refused.
categories.0x0c: queried when the effect menu opens; 118-byte {type, count} style body. Not decoded.
categories.0x0e: Line Out 1-4 trims: body[0] 01, body[1] link (00 linked), trims at body[2], [4], [6], [8] (frame.line_trim_command). The Monitor Out Trim is not here.
categories.0x11: index 0: 1 byte; index 1: 67 bytes. Not decoded.
categories.0x15: remaining AFX instances, {type, count} pairs (104 bytes). Not decoded further.
categories.0x16: mic emulations, 16 bytes (00 00 00 32 per preamp, unchanged by every panel gesture). Not decoded.
categories.0x17: reverb returns, 4 bytes, one per output mix: level | 0x80 mute (params.reverb_return).
categories.0x18: reverb sends, 66 bytes: header 00 20, then (send, pan) per strip 1-16.
categories.0x19: AFX strip order, 36 records of {type, inst} pairs, zero-padded. Record 0 is the mixer channel 1 (PREAMP 1) rack.

readback.category_counts_note: Each count is the highest index the vendor panel itself queried, plus one, identical across three connect walks. Categories 0x00 / 0x01 (firmware, identity with serial) are queried by the Manager Server, not the panel, and are left out until that capture is analysed.

state_report.notes: The device streams two unsolicited 320-byte reports at ~125 Hz each with no host traffic: magic 0x73 (state) and 0x83 (meter-like, mostly 0x60/0x32 lanes), the same pair as Zen Go. Unlike Zen Go, bytes 4..5 of 0x73 are 0x0000 (Zen Go: 0x4001). With the device at 48 kHz, 0x73 bytes 22..23 = 0xbb80 (48000) and byte 18 = 0x02 (the family's 48k index): candidates only, not tested against a rate change. Over 10 s idle, 0x73 offsets 160-163, 224-227, 242-243 moved. Base offsets deliberately not filled in.

Cabinet (type 4): not controllable from here and left unmapped. There is no small parameter block to edit; a cabinet can only be removed. Every other effect: a freshly loaded instance keeps the settings the device holds for it, which can differ from the vendor panel's defaults. Instances 0 and 1 are verified; the device has more. max_slots 4 is the Premium pack's FX instances per strip in the manual; three were seen loaded.
